correctness.rationale: The one-generation Hardy–Weinberg weighted-binomial update and strict monotonicity are derived explicitly. The exact two-epoch rational commutator factors as ab(a-b)x²(1-x)²U_h(x)²Q(x) divided by two strictly positive compositional denominators. For 0≤h≤1 Q(x)>0, and adjacent swaps plus monotone contexts prove the global extrema. For h>1 Q is a strictly concave quadratic with a unique root in (0,1) below the common fixed point, giving the sharp reversal. The package checker independently confirms symbolic identities and 673 exact assertions, not extrapolated finite proof.

value.rationale: The motivating finite-horizon genetic problem fixes environmental selection strengths but varies their timing. The result gives a strict, all-parameter optimum for every finite list rather than an approximation, and a sharp structural boundary caused by heterozygote advantage. Unlike the haploid multiplicative-odds case, diploid viability selection is frequency dependent. The overdominance counterexample explains when strong-first recommendations reverse, without empirical overclaims.
